title: a 21 year old started Render to create distribution-ready AI games
author: Antique-Raspberry551
selftext:
https://x.com/michaelgold3n/status/1800569521855779106?s=46

I believe that AI game dev for nontechnical folk is the future, and this kid seems to have conviction in his approach.

If not him, someone’s definitely going to win this race, especially as the tech gets better.

comments.author: Drakim
comments.body:
Before AI was at the scene, there was hype for an earlier concept called no-code. Rather than having to learn a complex programming language, you could just drag&drop in a convenient editor to get your gameplay.

This was touted as being The Future, after all, why bother learning to code for years and years if you could get it all for free with a no-code editor?

AI-generation editors are not the same as no-code editors, they have very different challenges and advantages. But I suspect that they do share one thing in common:

Designing a good game actually shares a lot of overlap with being a good developer. And if you can't put in the time to become a good developer, you likely aren't putting in the time to become a good game designer either. Balancing enemy stats, designing interesting loot drops, weighting damage vs armor vs life, planning out the downtime vs action ratio, and a million other things all require you to think, plan, calculate, and experiment. That means actually sitting down and putting a lot of hard work into your work. You won't be able to just tell the AI to "make it balanced" as the AI won't be playing the game, only writing code.

replies.author: Hey_Look_80085
replies.body:
Making games with AI will be the entertainment for the sake of it, and that will erode sales of games made the old fashioned way.

With every passing year someone will make even better AI assisted game development tools and the old way of doing things will become relics.

replies.author: Drakim
replies.body:
Confident predictions, but do you really think typing into a textbox about what you want your game to be like is gonna serious erode sales of games like World of Warcraft, Overwatch, and Call of Duty?

AI is obviously gonna get better and better, but you know what, so will video games (which will also be enhanced with AI technologies). I just seriously doubt that telling an AI what you want it to make will ever actually be more fun than playing a video game, for most people. It's like saying that nobody will ever want to read a book anymore because they can just talk to Siri.

> With every passing year someone will make even better AI assisted game development tools and the old way of doing things will become relics.

A world where AI is that powerful wouldn't be a world your recognize. You imagine our everyday lives right now except you don't have to learn programming as that's become a "relic" and you can just dictate to an AI what your video game should be like. But the truth is that if we had come that far, then nothing about human society would be the same anymore, it wouldn't just be our world + AI video games.
